s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with seizures, hemiparesis, and developmental delays
salient_findings: Upper motor neuron pattern of weakness
Focal abnormal brain activity on EEG
key_facts: Age of seizure onset: 3 months
Seizures have increased in frequency despite antiepileptic therapy
Delayed motor and cognitive milestones
Behavioral changes, including disturbed sleep and irritability
No family history of neurological disorders
No perinatal complications or trauma
Normal routine laboratory studies, including metabolic and infectious panels
EEG shows focal abnormal brain activity
MRI shows cerebral hemisphere atrophy and ex vacuo dilatation of the lateral ventricle
Ipsilateral calvarial thickening and compensatory hyperpneumatization of the sphenoid bone and bilateral mastoid air cells
Cystic encephalomalacia and gliosis in the right fronto-parieto-temporal region

shortlist.label: Rasmussen's encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic focal seizures, hemiparesis, and progressive neurological decline

shortlist.label: Hemimegalencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Hemiparesis, developmental delays, and cerebral hemisphere atrophy

shortlist.label: Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Cerebral hemiatrophy, calvarial thickening, and compensatory hyperpneumatization

shortlist.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Seizures, hemiparesis, and potential for cerebral atrophy

shortlist.label: Porencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic encephalomalacia and gliosis in the right fronto-parieto-temporal region

raw.rationale: The combination of cerebral hemisphere atrophy, ex vacuo dilatation of the lateral ventricle, ipsilateral calvarial thickening, and compensatory hyperpneumatization of the sphenoid bone and bilateral mastoid air cells, along with cystic encephalomalacia and gliosis, is most consistent with Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome, which is characterized by a remote focal brain injury leading to these specific imaging findings and associated neurological deficits.

rejected.label: Rasmussen's encephalitis
rejected.why: Rasmussen's encephalitis typically presents with more rapid progression of neurological deficits and inflammation on imaging, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Hemimegalencephaly
rejected.why: Hemimegalencephaly involves an overgrowth of one cerebral hemisphere, not atrophy, which contradicts the imaging findings in this case.

rejected.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
rejected.why: Sturge-Weber syndrome is characterized by a port-wine stain and leptomeningeal angiomatosis, which are not mentioned in the case description.

rejected.label: Porencephaly
rejected.why: Porencephaly refers to a cyst or cavity within the brain, often due to perinatal injury, but the combination of findings, especially the calvarial changes and hyperpneumatization, points more towards Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome.
